summary: Redwood AE and SE gave Atlas Retail a console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards and cost breakdown. Atlas highlighted three primary routes (customer support chat, product recommender, ingestion pipeline for embeddings) and asked about per-route cost attribution, alerting for regressions, and private deployment options. Redwood proposed a pilot with Dedicated capacity for the highest QPS route and showed how Console displays token-level cost, token breakdowns by model/variant, route-based dashboards, and recommendations from Redwood Optimize. Next steps: share pricing, security docs, and schedule pilot kickoff.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE. With me is Maya, our solutions engineer, and Liam from CS. How's everyone doing?

[00:07] Sofia Alvarez: Afternoon. Doing well, thanks. We have about 40 minutes, we want to see the Console, especially the cost breakdown per route and how you folks surface the analytics.

[00:15] Jordan Patel: Perfect, we'll jump in. Maya, want to share screen and start on the usage analytics tab?

[00:20] Maya Chen: Yep, sharing now. Alright, you should see the Console home. Quick note - some of the names are redacted for the demo but the flows are identical.

[00:33] Tom Reynolds: Can you slow down on the model catalog bit? We need to understand how you map model variants to routes.

[00:40] Maya Chen: Sure. On the left is 'Routes' - each route maps to a logical endpoint in your app. We show live QPS, p95 latency, and cost per minute. If you click into a route - for example, 'support-chat-prod' - we display a per-token cost breakdown, model usage, and a KV cache hit rate. Note - sometimes transcription in logs says 'KV cash' in older exports, that's just a typographic.

[01:10] Sofia Alvarez: For us the tricky part is attribution: we have three high-traffic routes - support chat, product recommender, and embeddings ingestion. We need to see how much each is costing daily and by model.

[01:20] Maya Chen: Totally. Here you can switch the view to 'Cost by route' - it aggregates tokens x model price and shows both total cost and unit cost per 1k tokens. There's also a breakdown by input vs output tokens so you can see where the spend is going.

[01:35] Ethan Moore: Do you break down costs by model variant? We might want to route support chat to a cheaper quantized variant and recommender to a larger model.

[01:42] Maya Chen: Yes. See the 'Model cost ladder' table - it lists active model variants used by that route, average token length, and the percent of traffic. You can click 'Optimize' to get recommendations - for example, 'Consider switching 18% of requests from model-x-32q to model-x-16q for cost saving with <2% quality delta'. That's from Redwood Optimize engine which analyzes your prompt sets and evals.

[02:05] Priya Singh: How accurate are the cost numbers? Do they include infra overhead for Dedicated?

[02:11] Jordan Patel: Good Q. The Console shows usage cost based on model pricing and token usage. For Dedicated/reserved capacity we also show amortized infra cost and committed discounts - that lives in the billing tab. For Hosted API it's pretty much per-token. If you choose Dedicated we'll run a cost model for your commit and show effective per-token cost including GPU amortization.

[02:28] Tom Reynolds: Is the per-route dashboard retroactive? We need 90 days of history for audits.

[02:33] Maya Chen: You can configure retention in org settings. By default we keep 30 days of full-resolution metrics and 12 months of aggregated metrics. There's an add-on for extended retention if you need 90 days with full traceability.

[02:45] Sofia Alvarez: What about alerts for cost spikes or regressions in quality? We had a bad incident where model drift spiked costs threefold.

[02:53] Maya Chen: Console has threshold alerts and anomaly detection. You can set an alert for token spend on a route or p95 latency. For quality regressions, we integrate with your eval sets - when you push a new model version, we run your eval prompts and surface regressions in the dashboard, plus automatic rollback policies if a canary fails.

[03:14] Priya Singh: Interesting. Can you show the 'deep-dive' view - token-level drilldown?

[03:20] Maya Chen: Sure - clicking into 'Token breakdown' shows sample requests, prompt/response token counts, and the exact pricing calc for that request. Here's an example: support-chat request at 10:12am - input 180 tokens, output 420 tokens, model-x-16q price $0.0008 per token, total $0.48. We also show cache hits so if the KV cache served 60% of tokens you see the discounted effective cost.

[03:46] Tom Reynolds: That cache percent - is that per customer session or global? We do per-customer prefix caching, so we need per-tenant view.

[03:54] Maya Chen: There is a 'split by tenant' filter. You can tag routes with tenancy or pass a customer_id header and Console will attribute usage. Works for multi-tenant setups.

[04:06] Jordan Patel: Also, for private deployments, all telemetry can be forwarded to your SIEM/VPC endpoint so you don't need to push PII out of your network.

[04:14] Sofia Alvarez: Good. On security - we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS integration, and audit logs. Maya?

[04:20] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO, RBAC at route and project level, KMS for key management, and full audit logs. I'll share the SOC2 + ISO documents after the call. For private/on-prem we provide a control plane option where logs remain in your VPC; for fully air-gapped deployments we have an on-prem package.

[04:40] Ethan Moore: One more on routing policies - can we set rules that route based on latency requirements? Example: 100ms SLO for checkout suggestions, fallback to cheaper model if latency breaches.

[04:50] Maya Chen: Yes - routing policies allow rule-based routing by latency, cost, or region. You can set primary model and a fallback variant. There's also automated fallback if Dedicated capacity runs low - requests can spill to hosted or to a smaller model variant.

[05:05] Tom Reynolds: What's the granularity on the cost forecasting? We need a weekly roll-up and also an estimate for holiday peaks.

[05:12] Maya Chen: Forecasting uses historical usage and seasonality. You can simulate a 2x or 3x spike and Console will estimate cost and required capacity; for Dedicated it will propose autoscale policies and burst options.

[05:26] Sofia Alvarez: Can we export cost by route to our FinOps system? CSV or API?

[05:31] Maya Chen: Both. There's an API endpoint for per-route billing exports and you can schedule CSV email exports daily/weekly. We also support direct Snowflake connectors for analytics.

[05:42] Priya Singh: Let's talk pilot. We want to bench the support-chat route which is highest QPS. What's implied SLA during a pilot and what data do you need from us?

[05:52] Jordan Patel: For a pilot we can offer a week-long Dedicated trial or a Hosted benchmarking window. Recommended: give us your traffic profile (qps distribution by hour), sample prompts, and target latency/SLOs. Maya will run a bench using our runtime and provide a performance + cost report.

[06:08] Maya Chen: If you can share sample traffic by route and a few representative prompts, we'll run canary loads and include KV-cache optimizations. Also tell us expected peak concurrency and average request size.

[06:18] Tom Reynolds: I'll pull that - backlog has some telemetry dumps. I can anonymize and share.

[06:23] Ethan Moore: How do rollouts show up in Console? We want to do canary and A/B on model versions.

[06:29] Maya Chen: Rollouts appear in the 'Deployments' tab - you can configure weight-based canaries, automatic rollback on latency or eval regression thresholds, and compare side-by-side metrics. There is also a diff view of cost impact per model version.

[06:42] Sofia Alvarez: Any gotchas with embeddings/ingestion pipelines? We have a high-volume embedding job that runs every night.

[06:49] Maya Chen: For batch ingestion we recommend a different throughput profile - using our bulk ingestion path with larger sequence lengths and larger batch sizes, plus quantized models where appropriate. Console shows a 'Batch jobs' view with cost per embedding and aggregate throughput. You can also schedule jobs to run in off-peak windows to reduce cost.

[07:05] Priya Singh: You mentioned Optimize recommendations earlier - can you show an example?

[07:10] Maya Chen: Sure - in 'Optimize' module, you upload a small eval set or connect to your existing evals. This example run shows recommended quantization, batching configuration (e.g., batch size 32 for embeddings), and a cost savings estimate. For this demo it suggests switching 25% of recommender traffic to a smaller model with <1.5% MRR impact.

[07:33] Tom Reynolds: Is the Optimize engine model-agnostic? We use a mix of open models and internally-tuned variants.

[07:39] Maya Chen: It's model-agnostic - it uses observed token distributions and your eval outputs to recommend quantization, batching, and routing. For private models you can still run Optimize locally if you prefer.

[07:50] Jordan Patel: Quick check - any regulatory constraints we should know about? Data residency, restricted PII flow?

[07:56] Sofia Alvarez: We need EU residency for EU customers and some logs redacted for PII.

[08:01] Maya Chen: We have region controls and redaction features. For PII, we can configurable maskers at ingestion and route-level filters; logs forwarded to your SIEM will have PII stripped if you enable that.

[08:12] Ethan Moore: Quick question - pricing examples you showed earlier, can you put a sample for support-chat?

[08:17] Jordan Patel: Yankee example - support-chat at 100k requests/day with avg 600 tokens per request yields ~60M tokens/day. On Hosted at $0.0008 per token that's roughly $48k/day - obviously that's rough. With Dedicated/commit you'd see big reductions; Maya will model that based on your traffic and target commit.

[08:40] Tom Reynolds: That Hosted number is high; can you explain where cost drops with Dedicated?

[08:44] Maya Chen: Dedicated gives GPU amortization and discounting - for example a committed pool for that route could cut effective per-token by 40-60% depending on utilization. Also caching and batching reduce emitted tokens. In our earlier examples, adding prefix cache for support chat reduced output tokens by 35% on average.

[09:03] Priya Singh: One more operational question - how do we detect token leakage in prompts? We've had hidden context causing larger token counts.

[09:11] Maya Chen: Console has a 'Prompt inspector' that surfaces avg prompt sizes and shows outliers. You can set alerts for sudden jumps in avg input tokens. We can also annotate sample traces where prompts grew unexpectedly.

[09:25] Jordan Patel: Sounds like we're near the end - any remaining blockers?

[09:29] Sofia Alvarez: We need to review security docs and a pricing model. Also want to schedule the pilot kickoff for next week.

[09:36] Jordan Patel: Got it - action items: Jordan send pricing, Maya send SOC2 and deployment checklist, Tom send traffic profile. We'll propose two pilot windows (11/20, 11/24).

[09:47] Tom Reynolds: I can do 11/20 morning.

[09:50] Priya Singh: 11/24 I might be out, but 11/20 works.

[09:54] Jordan Patel: Great - we'll follow up in email with proposed times. Thanks everyone.

[10:00] Maya Chen: Thanks!

[10:02] End of recording.

Notes: Transcript contains occasional minor transcription errors (e.g., 'KV cash' vs 'KV cache'); speaker labels include roles for clarity. The call included a live Console demo and links referenced: /docs/soc2, /docs/deploy-checklist, /demo/bench-report (links to be shared after call).
